q: A Central Government office located in Region 'C' issued 200 letters during a quarter, of which 110 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 40 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 75 per cent
options.C: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' being 55 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'C'

e: 110 of 200 letters is 55 per cent. The Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region C is 55 per cent, so the office has just met the target.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'B' issued 300 letters during a quarter, of which 240 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B' being 90 per cent
options.B: The office has met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 75 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 55 per cent
options.D: The office has met the target, no percentage being prescribed for Region 'B'

e: 240 of 300 letters is 80 per cent. The Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region B is 90 per cent, so the office has fallen short.

q: A clerk in a divisional accounts office passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 58 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.B: Rs 800
options.D: No cash award, the minimum marks required being 60 per cent

e: Under the Hindi Teaching Scheme, the Pragya cash award is Rs 800 for 55 to 59 per cent marks, Rs 1,600 for 60 to 69 per cent and Rs 2,400 for 70 per cent or more; 58 per cent falls in the first slab.

q: A senior clerk passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 75 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 800

e: The Pragya cash award slab for 70 per cent or more marks is Rs 2,400; 75 per cent falls in that top slab.

q: A typist in a Central Government office passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 87 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 90 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 85 per cent marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Pragya examination in the same year
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 24 months instead

e: A cash award for the Hindi typewriting examination is admissible only on securing 90 per cent or more marks; 87 per cent is below that threshold, so no award is payable.

q: A stenographer passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 95 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 98 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if his stenography speed exceeds 100 words per minute
options.C: He becomes entitled to a lumpsum award in lieu of the cash award
options.D: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold of 88 per cent or more marks for the stenography examination having been secured

e: A cash award for the Hindi stenography examination is admissible on securing 88 per cent or more marks; 95 per cent crosses that threshold, so the award is payable.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 28 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He passes, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 25 words per minute
options.B: He does not pass on speed, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination being 30 words per minute
options.C: He passes, the examination being decided on marks alone and not on speed
options.D: He passes only if he secures 90 per cent marks in the Pragya examination

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is 30 words per minute; 28 words per minute is below it, so the candidate does not pass on speed.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 85 words per minute. As regards the prescribed speed standard, the correct position is:

options.A: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 100 words per minute
options.B: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 120 words per minute
options.C: He meets the prescribed speed standard only if he also attains 30 words per minute in Hindi typewriting
options.D: He meets the prescribed speed standard, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination being 80 words per minute

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is 80 words per minute; 85 words per minute meets that standard.

q: A 34-year-old employee, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 40 years
options.B: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.C: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years
options.D: He must undergo the training only after attaining the age of 45 years

e: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained 45 years of age; a 34-year-old without that knowledge must undergo it.

q: An employee aged 47 years, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is proposed to be nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: In-service Hindi training is not compulsory for him, he having attained the age of 45 years
options.B: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for him irrespective of his age
options.C: He must undergo the training only if his office is notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976
options.D: He must undergo the training only if he is posted in Region 'C'

e: In-service Hindi training ceases to be compulsory once an employee attains 45 years of age; at 47 years he is not compulsorily nominable, even without working knowledge of Hindi.

q: In a newly formed Central Government office, 76 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi, and the head of office proposes its notification. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 75 per cent or more
options.B: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi
options.C: The office can be notified, notification depending only on the total number of staff
options.D: The office can be notified only with the approval of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language

e: An office can be notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 only when 80 per cent or more of its staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi; 76 per cent is short of that proportion.

q: In a Central Government office, 82 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 90 per cent or more
options.B: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 85 per cent or more
options.C: Notification is not permissible for offices located in Region 'B'
options.D: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi

e: Rule 10(4) notification requires 80 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi; 82 per cent satisfies that proportion, so the office can be notified.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 7,500 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.B: He becomes eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 5,000 words in a year
options.C: He becomes eligible for consideration only if he repeats the performance in the following year
options.D: He is eligible only if his office is located in Region 'A'

e: Eligibility for the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi requires at least 10,000 words in a year; 7,500 words falls below the minimum, so the employee is not eligible for consideration.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 12,500 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 20,000 words in a year
options.B: He is eligible for consideration only if the noting was done in an office notified under Rule 10(4)
options.C: He becomes eligible for consideration for the cash award, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.D: He is not eligible for consideration, the scheme applying only to noting done in Region 'A' offices

e: The minimum for consideration under the noting and drafting incentive scheme is 10,000 words of Hindi noting and drafting in a year; 12,500 words exceeds it, so the employee is eligible for consideration.

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the eighth month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 6 months only
options.B: The claim is in order only if the employee passes the examination again
options.C: The claim is in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 12 months
options.D: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible only from the thirteenth month onwards

e: Personal pay equal to one increment, granted on passing the prescribed Hindi examination, is admissible for 12 months; the eighth month is within that period, so the claim is in order.

q: A Zonal Railway office issues a permit under the Official Languages Act framework in English only, and the dealing clerk contends that a permit need not be issued bilingually. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct, permits being outside Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.B: The contention is correct if the permit is issued in Region 'C'
options.C: The contention is correct if a Hindi version is supplied later on demand
options.D: The contention is not correct; a permit is among the documents specified in Section 3(3) which must be issued in both Hindi and English, the responsibility resting with the officer signing the document

e: A permit is a document specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 and must be issued in both Hindi and English; the signing officer is responsible for ensuring this.

q: A Central Government office receives a letter written in Hindi. The dealing assistant proposes to reply in English, contending that the language of the reply is a matter of his discretion. The correct position is:

options.A: The proposal is in order, the reply being permissible in either language
options.B: The proposal is in order if the office is located in Region 'C'
options.C: The proposal is not in order; a letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi, the target for such replies being 100 per cent
options.D: The proposal is in order if a Hindi translation is kept on the file

e: A letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi under the Official Language Rules, with a 100 per cent target for such replies; the language of reply is not at the dealing assistant discretion.

q: A Central Government office is located at Jaipur in the State of Rajasthan. The target prescribed under the Annual Programme for correspondence originating in Hindi from that office is:

options.A: 100 per cent, Rajasthan being placed in Region 'A'
options.B: 90 per cent, Rajasthan being placed in Region 'B'
options.C: 55 per cent, Rajasthan being placed in Region 'C'
options.D: 30 per cent, as for noting on files

e: Rajasthan is a Region A State, and the Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi from Region A offices is 100 per cent.

q: A Central Government office is located at Kochi in the State of Kerala. The target prescribed under the Annual Programme for correspondence originating in Hindi from that office is:

options.A: 100 per cent, Kerala being placed in Region 'A'
options.B: 55 per cent, Kerala being placed in Region 'C'
options.C: 90 per cent, Kerala being placed in Region 'B'
options.D: No target, Kerala being outside all regions

e: Kerala is a Region C State, and the Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi from Region C offices is 55 per cent.

q: A Central Government office is located at Pune in the State of Maharashtra. The target prescribed under the Annual Programme for correspondence originating in Hindi from that office is:

options.A: 55 per cent, Maharashtra being placed in Region 'C'
options.B: 100 per cent, Maharashtra being placed in Region 'A'
options.C: 75 per cent, Maharashtra being placed in Region 'B'
options.D: 90 per cent, Maharashtra being placed in Region 'B'

e: Maharashtra is a Region B State, and the Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi from Region B offices is 90 per cent.

q: During a quarter, a Central Government office recorded 60 notes on files, of which 18 were written in Hindi. With reference to the target fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short, the prescribed target for noting in Hindi being 50 per cent
options.B: The office has met the target, the prescribed target for noting on files in Hindi being 30 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target being 10 per cent
options.D: No target is fixed for noting on files in Hindi

e: 18 of 60 notes is 30 per cent. The Annual Programme target for noting on files in Hindi is 30 per cent, so the office has met the target.

q: For its Quarterly Progress Report, an office counts its Hindi correspondence. During the quarter it issued 50 letters, of which 20 were originally written in Hindi and 30 were English drafts translated into Hindi before issue. The number to be counted as Hindi correspondence is:
e: Only letters originally written in Hindi count as Hindi correspondence for the Quarterly Progress Report; English drafts merely translated into Hindi do not count, so only the 20 original letters count.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Meetings of the Town Official Language Implementation Committee are normally held twice a year.
2. Meetings of the Official Language Implementation Committee of a Central Government office are normally held every quarter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both are correct: Town Official Language Implementation Committee meetings are normally held twice a year, while an office Official Language Implementation Committee normally meets every quarter.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Official Language Rules, 1976 have been framed by the Central Government in exercise of the powers conferred by Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963.
2. The Official Language Rules, 1976 do not apply to the State of Tamil Nadu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Official Language Rules, 1976 were framed under Section 8 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, and they extend to the whole of India except the State of Tamil Nadu.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 4 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, it is the duty of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language to review the progress made in the use of Hindi for the official purposes of the Union and to submit a report to the President, with recommendations.
2. The members of that Committee are elected by the members of the two Houses of Parliament in accordance with the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Section 4 of the 1963 Act charges the Committee of Parliament on Official Language with reviewing the progress of Hindi and reporting to the President, and its members are elected by proportional representation through the single transferable vote.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya, meant for employees who cannot attend regular training classes, are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate.
2. Besides translation of codes, manuals and other non-statutory material, the Central Translation Bureau also conducts translation training programmes for the translators of Central Government offices.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya correspondence courses are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate, and the Central Translation Bureau also runs translation training programmes besides translating codes, manuals and non-statutory material.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. World Hindi Day is observed on 10th January every year, commemorating the holding of the First World Hindi Conference at Nagpur in January 1975.
2. Hindi Pakhwada is observed in Central Government offices and Railways from 14th September to 28th September every year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: World Hindi Day on 10 January marks the First World Hindi Conference held at Nagpur in January 1975, and Hindi Pakhwada is observed from 14 to 28 September each year.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kendriya Hindi Sansthan (Central Institute of Hindi) at Agra is mainly engaged in teaching Hindi to non-Hindi speaking Indian and foreign learners, training of Hindi teachers and research in Hindi.
2. 'Rajbhasha Bharati', the quarterly journal devoted to the Official Language and its implementation, is published by the Department of Official Language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both are correct: the Kendriya Hindi Sansthan at Agra teaches Hindi to non-Hindi speaking and foreign learners, trains Hindi teachers and does research, and Rajbhasha Bharati is the quarterly journal of the Department of Official Language.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The speed prescribed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is 30 words per minute.
2. The speed prescribed for passing the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme is 100 words per minute.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: the Hindi typewriting pass speed is 30 words per minute, while the Hindi stenography pass speed is 80 words per minute, not 100.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A cash award of Rs 2,400 is admissible to an employee who passes the Pragya examination with 70 per cent or more marks.
2. A cash award for passing the Hindi typewriting examination is admissible on securing 95 per cent or more marks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Rs 2,400 is the Pragya award for 70 per cent or more marks, but the typewriting award threshold is 90 per cent or more marks, not 95 per cent.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Central Government office can be notified under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 when 80 per cent or more of its staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi.
2. The Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi is sent by a Central Government office directly to the President's Secretariat every quarter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Rule 10(4) notification needs 80 per cent or more staff with working knowledge of Hindi. Quarterly Progress Reports go to the controlling office or Ministry, not to the President Secretariat.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Article 350B of the Constitution provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, appointed by the President.
2. Article 350A of the Constitution relates to facilities for instruction in the mother tongue at the primary stage to children belonging to linguistic minority groups.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Article 350B provides for a Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities appointed by the President, and Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage for linguistic minority children.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 348(1) of the Constitution, until Parliament by law otherwise provides, the authoritative texts of all Bills introduced in Parliament or in a State Legislature, and of all Acts passed and Ordinances promulgated, shall be in English.
2. A translation in Hindi of a Central Act, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, is only a summary for the guidance of officers and not the authoritative text.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: 1 only

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Article 348(1) keeps authoritative texts of Bills, Acts and Ordinances in English until Parliament provides otherwise. A Hindi translation of a Central Act published under the President authority is deemed the authoritative Hindi text, so statement 2 is wrong.

q: A newly opened Central Government office asks where it is required to send its Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: Directly to the Committee of Parliament on Official Language
options.B: To its controlling office / administrative Ministry or Department
options.C: To the President's Secretariat
options.D: To the Union Public Service Commission

e: A Central Government office sends its Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi to its controlling office or administrative Ministry or Department, which consolidates and forwards it.

q: An employee has passed the Matriculation examination with Hindi as the medium of examination. On that ground alone, under the Official Language Rules, 1976, he shall be deemed to have acquired:

options.A: Proficiency in Hindi
options.B: Neither working knowledge nor proficiency in Hindi
options.C: Working knowledge of Hindi
options.D: Both proficiency and working knowledge of Hindi

e: Under the Rules, a person who has passed Matriculation with Hindi as the medium of examination is deemed to have proficiency in Hindi; medium, not Hindi as a mere subject, is the test for proficiency.

q: A group of employees of a Central Government office possess knowledge of Hindi but hesitate to do noting and drafting in Hindi in their day-to-day work. The programme organised primarily to give such employees practical training in doing noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi is:

options.A: A Hindi workshop (Hindi Karyashala)
options.B: A translation training programme of the Central Translation Bureau
options.C: The Prabodh correspondence course
options.D: A meeting of the Town Official Language Implementation Committee

e: Hindi workshops, or Hindi Karyashala, are organised precisely to give employees who know Hindi practical training and confidence in doing noting, drafting and other official work in Hindi.

q: While setting up new computers in a Central Government office for Hindi (Devanagari) typing, the standard keyboard layout prescribed, as per the Bureau of Indian Standards standard adopted for the purpose, to be used is:

options.A: The Remington typewriter layout only
options.B: A phonetic layout designed by the office for itself
options.C: The English QWERTY layout with stickers pasted on the keys
options.D: InScript

e: InScript is the standard keyboard layout for Hindi Devanagari typing, based on the Bureau of Indian Standards standard adopted for computers in Central Government offices.

q: A new station building is being provided with name boards, designation boards and sign boards. The three languages must appear on these boards in the order:

options.A: Hindi, English, Regional language
options.B: Regional language, Hindi, English
options.C: English, Hindi, Regional language
options.D: Regional language, English, Hindi

e: On name boards, designation boards and sign boards, the order of languages is regional language first, then Hindi, then English.

q: A Central Government office is getting a revised procedural manual printed for issue to all its field units. Under the Official Language Rules, the manual must be printed and published:

options.A: In Hindi only
options.B: In English only
options.C: In diglot form, i.e., in Hindi and English
options.D: In the regional language only

e: Under the Official Language Rules, manuals and other procedural literature must be printed and published in diglot form, that is in both Hindi and English.

q: On the creation of a new Zonal Railway, the officer at its headquarters to be designated for looking after the work relating to implementation of the Official Language Policy is the:

options.A: Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari (Chief Official Language Officer)
options.B: Divisional Railway Manager
options.C: Senior Divisional Personnel Officer
options.D: Chief Commercial Manager

e: At a Zonal Railway headquarters, the Mukhya Rajbhasha Adhikari, or Chief Official Language Officer, is designated to look after implementation of the Official Language Policy.

q: A Division located in Region 'B' is adjudged the best (Adarsh) Division on Indian Railways for excellence in implementation of the Official Language Policy. The running shield admissible for the Division is:

options.A: The Acharya Raghuveer Running Shield
options.B: The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield for Region 'C' divisions
options.C: The Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield
options.D: No running shield exists for divisions in Region 'B'

e: The running shield for the best, or Adarsh, Division in Region B for Official Language implementation is the Acharya Mahaveer Prasad Running Shield; the Raghuveer shield belongs to a different region category.

q: Official correspondence is to be exchanged between the Government of one State and the Government of another State. Under Article 346 of the Constitution, the language to be used for such communication is:

options.A: Hindi in Devanagari script only
options.B: The regional language of the State which receives the communication
options.C: The language for the time being authorised for use in the Union for its official purposes
options.D: The language spoken by the majority in the two States

e: Article 346 provides that the language authorised for use in the Union for official purposes is also the language for communication between one State and another, and between a State and the Union.

q: A language is spoken by a substantial proportion of the population of a State, and that section of the population desires its official recognition. Under Article 347 of the Constitution, on being satisfied in this regard, the authority who may direct that the language shall also be officially recognised throughout the State or any part thereof for specified purposes is:

options.A: The Governor of the State
options.B: The President
options.C: The Chief Minister of the State
options.D: The Official Language Commission

e: Under Article 347, the President, on being satisfied that a substantial proportion of a State population desires recognition of their language, may direct its official recognition for specified purposes in that State or part of it.

q: On the occasion of Hindi Diwas, the employees of a Central Government office assemble and take:

options.A: An oath of secrecy
options.B: A pledge to pass the Hindi typing examination
options.C: The national pledge only
options.D: The Rajbhasha pledge (Rajbhasha Pratigya), to use Hindi to the maximum possible extent in their official work

e: On Hindi Diwas, employees take the Rajbhasha Pratigya, the Official Language pledge, to use Hindi to the maximum possible extent in their official work.

q: An employee passes the prescribed Pragya examination through his own efforts, by self-study, without undergoing the prescribed training. The incentive admissible to him under the scheme is:

options.A: A lumpsum award
options.B: Out-of-turn promotion to the next grade
options.C: Additional casual leave of fifteen days
options.D: No incentive, incentives being admissible only after undergoing training

e: An employee who passes the prescribed Pragya examination by self-study, without undergoing the prescribed training, is entitled to a lumpsum award as the incentive for that effort.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'A' issued 400 letters during a quarter, of which 376 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'A' being 90 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'A' being 100 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'A' being 75 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'A'

e: 376 of 400 letters is 94 per cent. The Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region A is 100 per cent, so the office has fallen short.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'C' issued 600 letters during a quarter, of which 330 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' being 55 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 75 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 40 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'C'

e: 330 of 600 letters is 55 per cent. The Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region C is 55 per cent, so the office has just met the target.

q: A Central Government office located in Region 'B' issued 200 letters during a quarter, of which 190 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 100 per cent
options.B: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 95 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B' being 90 per cent
options.D: The office has met the target, no percentage being prescribed for Region 'B'

e: 190 of 200 letters is 95 per cent. The Annual Programme target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region B is 90 per cent, so the office has exceeded the target.

q: During a quarter, a Central Government office recorded 80 notes on files, of which 16 were written in Hindi. With reference to the target fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi, the position is:

options.A: The office has met the target, the prescribed target for noting in Hindi being 30 per cent
options.B: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target being 10 per cent
options.C: No target is fixed for noting on files in Hindi
options.D: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for noting on files in Hindi being 30 per cent

e: 16 of 80 notes is 20 per cent. The Annual Programme target for noting on files in Hindi is 30 per cent, so the office has fallen short of the target.

q: A clerk in a zonal accounts office passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 62 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 800
options.D: No cash award, the minimum marks required being 70 per cent

e: The Pragya cash award is Rs 1,600 for 60 to 69 per cent marks; 62 per cent falls in that middle slab, between the Rs 800 and Rs 2,400 slabs.

q: An accounts assistant passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 59 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.C: Rs 800
options.D: No cash award, the minimum marks required being 60 per cent

e: The Pragya cash award is Rs 800 for 55 to 59 per cent marks; 59 per cent falls in that lowest award slab.

q: A typist in a Central Government office passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 96 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 98 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Pragya examination in the same year
options.C: He becomes entitled to a lumpsum award in lieu of the cash award
options.D: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold of 90 per cent or more marks for the typewriting examination having been secured

e: A cash award for the Hindi typewriting examination is admissible on securing 90 per cent or more marks; 96 per cent crosses that threshold, so the award is payable.

q: A stenographer passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 85 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the stenography examination being 88 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 80 per cent marks
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if his stenography speed exceeds 100 words per minute
options.D: He becomes entitled to personal pay for a period of 12 months instead

e: A cash award for the Hindi stenography examination is admissible only on securing 88 per cent or more marks; 85 per cent is below that threshold, so no award is payable.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 34 words per minute. The correct position is:

options.A: He does not pass on speed, the prescribed speed for passing the examination being 35 words per minute
options.B: He passes on speed, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination being 30 words per minute
options.C: He does not pass, the examination being decided on marks alone and not on speed
options.D: He passes only if he secures 90 per cent marks in the Pragya examination

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi typewriting examination is 30 words per minute; 34 words per minute exceeds it, so the candidate passes on speed.

q: A candidate appears in the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme and attains a speed of 75 words per minute. As regards the prescribed speed standard, the correct position is:

options.A: He meets the prescribed speed standard, the prescribed speed being 70 words per minute
options.B: He meets the prescribed speed standard only if he also attains 30 words per minute in Hindi typewriting
options.C: He falls short, the prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination being 80 words per minute
options.D: He falls short, the prescribed speed being 120 words per minute

e: The prescribed speed for passing the Hindi stenography examination is 80 words per minute; 75 words per minute falls short of that standard.

q: A 41-year-old employee, who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi, is nominated for in-service Hindi training under the Hindi Teaching Scheme. The correct position is:

options.A: He must undergo the training, in-service Hindi training being compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained the age of 45 years
options.B: He is exempt, in-service Hindi training not being compulsory after the age of 40 years
options.C: He must undergo the training only if his office is located in Region 'A'
options.D: He must undergo the training only after attaining the age of 45 years

e: In-service Hindi training is compulsory for an employee who does not possess working knowledge of Hindi and has not attained 45 years of age; a 41-year-old without that knowledge must undergo it.

q: In a newly formed Central Government office, 79 per cent of the staff have acquired working knowledge of Hindi, and the head of office proposes its notification. The correct position regarding notification of the office under Rule 10(4) of the Official Language Rules, 1976 is:

options.A: The office can be notified, the prescribed proportion being 75 per cent or more
options.B: The office can be notified, notification depending only on the total number of staff
options.C: The office can be notified only with the approval of the Committee of Parliament on Official Language
options.D: The office cannot be notified, the prescribed proportion being 80 per cent or more of the staff having acquired working knowledge of Hindi

e: Rule 10(4) notification requires 80 per cent or more of the staff to have acquired working knowledge of Hindi; 79 per cent, though close, is below that proportion, so the office cannot be notified.

q: An employee does noting and drafting in Hindi of 8,500 words during a year and claims consideration for a cash award under the incentive scheme for original noting and drafting in Hindi. The correct position is:

options.A: He becomes eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being 5,000 words in a year
options.B: He is not eligible for consideration, the prescribed minimum being at least 10,000 words of noting and drafting in Hindi in a year
options.C: He becomes eligible for consideration only if he repeats the performance in the following year
options.D: He is eligible only if his office is located in Region 'A'

e: Eligibility for the noting and drafting incentive scheme requires at least 10,000 words of Hindi noting and drafting in a year; 8,500 words falls below the minimum, so the employee is not eligible.

q: An employee who was granted personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination claims its continuance in the sixteenth month after the grant. The correct position is:

options.A: The claim is in order, personal pay being admissible for an indefinite period
options.B: The claim is in order only if the employee passes the examination again
options.C: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible for a period of 12 months only
options.D: The claim is not in order, personal pay being admissible only from the thirteenth month onwards

e: Personal pay equal to one increment on passing the prescribed Hindi examination is admissible for 12 months only; a claim in the sixteenth month is beyond that period and not in order.

q: For its Quarterly Progress Report, an office counts its Hindi correspondence. During the quarter it issued 80 letters, of which 35 were originally written in Hindi and 45 were English drafts translated into Hindi before issue. The number to be counted as Hindi correspondence is:
e: Only letters originally written in Hindi count as Hindi correspondence; English drafts translated into Hindi before issue are excluded, so only the 35 original letters count.

q: A Zonal Railway office executes a contract with a firm and issues it in English only, the dealing clerk contending that a contract need not be issued bilingually. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct, contracts being outside Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.B: The contention is not correct; a contract is among the documents specified in Section 3(3) which must be issued in both Hindi and English, the responsibility resting with the officer signing the document
options.C: The contention is correct if the contract is executed in Region 'C'
options.D: The contention is correct if a Hindi version is supplied later on demand

e: A contract is a document specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 and must be issued in both Hindi and English; the signing officer is responsible for ensuring this.

q: A Central Government office adopts a resolution and issues it in Hindi only, contending that issue in one language is sufficient since Hindi is the Official Language of the Union. The correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct, resolutions being outside Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963
options.B: The contention is correct if the resolution is issued in Region 'A'
options.C: The contention is correct if an English version is kept on the file
options.D: The contention is not correct; a resolution is among the documents specified in Section 3(3) which must be issued in both Hindi and English

e: A resolution is a document specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 and must be issued in both Hindi and English; issue in Hindi alone does not satisfy the section.

q: A divisional accounts office located in Region 'C' receives a letter written in Hindi from another Central Government office. The dealing assistant proposes to reply in English, contending that offices in Region 'C' may reply in English. The correct position is:

options.A: The proposal is not in order; a letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi, the target for such replies being 100 per cent, irrespective of the region in which the office is located
options.B: The proposal is in order, the reply being permissible in either language
options.C: The proposal is in order if a Hindi translation is kept on the file
options.D: The proposal is in order during quarters other than the one in which the Quarterly Progress Report is sent

e: A letter received in Hindi must be replied to in Hindi, with a 100 per cent target for such replies, whatever region the receiving office is in; Region C location gives no liberty to reply in English.

q: A Central Government office issues a communication in Hindi to an office located in Region 'C'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The communication must be issued in English only
options.B: No accompaniment is required with the communication
options.C: The communication must be accompanied by its English translation
options.D: The communication must be accompanied by a translation in the regional language of Region 'C'

e: Under the Official Language Rules, a communication issued in Hindi to an office in Region C must be accompanied by its English translation, so that the receiving office can deal with it.

q: A Central Government office issues a communication in English to an office located in Region 'A'. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the correct position is:

options.A: The communication must be re-issued in the regional language
options.B: The communication must be accompanied by its Hindi translation
options.C: No accompaniment is required with the communication
options.D: The communication is barred altogether, English not being permissible for Region 'A'

e: Under the Official Language Rules, a communication issued in English to an office in Region A must be accompanied by its Hindi translation.

q: An employee of a Central Government office records his noting on a file in Hindi. His superior officer asks him to also furnish a Hindi-to-English translation of the noting for the officer's convenience. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976:

options.A: The employee must furnish the translation on demand
options.B: Only a gazetted officer can be asked for such a translation
options.C: The translation has to be prepared by the Hindi Translator at the employee's cost
options.D: The employee cannot be required to furnish a translation of his noting in the other language

e: Under the Official Language Rules, an employee who records noting in Hindi cannot be required to furnish a translation of that noting into English for a superior convenience.

q: A newly opened branch of a Central Government office gets fresh rubber stamps prepared for use in its sections. Under the Rajbhasha implementation instructions, the rubber stamps should be prepared:

options.A: In bilingual form, i.e., in Hindi and English
options.B: In English only, as stamps are internal stationery
options.C: In the regional language only
options.D: In Hindi only, without exception

e: Rubber stamps used in Central Government offices are to be prepared in bilingual form, in Hindi and English, like other official stationery and forms.

q: A Central Government office wishes to release an advertisement in newspapers only in English, contending that advertisements are meant for the educated public. In accordance with the Official Language Policy, the correct position is:

options.A: The contention is correct, advertisements being outside the Official Language Policy
options.B: The advertisement should be released only in the regional language newspaper of the area
options.C: The advertisement should be released in Hindi and English, i.e., in both Hindi and English newspapers
options.D: The advertisement should be released only in Hindi newspapers during Hindi Pakhwada and in English newspapers otherwise

e: Advertisements of Central Government offices are to be released in both Hindi and English newspapers, so that the publicity reaches readers of both language streams.

q: At a railway divisional office, a member of the public makes a telephone enquiry in Hindi. The official attending the call insists on replying in English, contending that official replies must always be in English. The correct position is that the official should, as far as possible, reply to him:

options.A: In English only, telephone replies being official communications
options.B: In Hindi
options.C: Only after transferring the call to the Hindi Cell
options.D: In the regional language of the office

e: A public enquiry made in Hindi on the telephone should, as far as possible, be answered in Hindi; the caller language governs the reply, not a supposed rule that replies must be in English.

q: A Central Government office maintains its website in English only and proposes to continue it in that form. The correct position under the Official Language Policy is:

options.A: The website may continue in English only, websites being outside the policy
options.B: The website should be maintained in the regional language only
options.C: The website should be maintained in Hindi only
options.D: The website is required to be maintained in Hindi and English, i.e., in bilingual form

e: Websites of Central Government offices are required to be maintained in bilingual form, in Hindi and English; an English-only website does not meet the Official Language Policy.

q: A Central Government office procures a software package which has the facility of working in English only, for use in its sections. The correct position is:

options.A: Software packages procured for use in Central Government offices are required to have the facility of working in Hindi as well, i.e., bilingual (Hindi-English) capability
options.B: The package is in order, Hindi work being done only on typewriters
options.C: The package is in order if it works in the regional language of the State of posting
options.D: The package is in order only during Hindi Pakhwada

e: Software packages procured for Central Government offices are required to have bilingual Hindi-English capability, so that official work in Hindi can be done on them.

q: A Central Government office gets its letter-heads printed in Hindi only for use in official correspondence. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the letter-heads are required to be printed in:

options.A: Hindi only
options.B: English only
options.C: Hindi and English
options.D: The regional language only

e: Under the Official Language Rules, letter-heads of Central Government offices are required to be printed in both Hindi and English, not in Hindi alone.

q: A Central Government office gets the headings of the registers used in its sections printed in English only. Under the Official Language Rules, 1976, the headings of registers are required to be printed in:

options.A: English only
options.B: Hindi and English (bilingual)
options.C: Hindi only
options.D: The regional language only

e: Under the Official Language Rules, headings of registers used in sections must be printed in bilingual form, in Hindi and English.

q: A Central Government office has to correspond with the embassy of a foreign country in India in connection with an official matter. The correspondence is to be conducted in:

options.A: Hindi only
options.B: Hindi and English both, as in Section 3(3) documents
options.C: The official language of that foreign country
options.D: English

e: Correspondence with a foreign embassy in India is conducted in English, the accepted language for such external communication, and not as a Section 3(3) bilingual document.

q: A group of Central Government employees, who cannot attend the regular Hindi training classes held during office hours, wish to learn Hindi for passing the prescribed examinations. The correspondence courses in Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya meant for such employees are conducted by:

options.A: The Central Hindi Directorate
options.B: The Central Hindi Training Institute
options.C: The Central Translation Bureau
options.D: The Kendriya Hindi Samiti

e: The Prabodh, Praveen and Pragya correspondence courses for employees who cannot attend regular classes are conducted by the Central Hindi Directorate.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 349 of the Constitution, during the first fifteen years from the commencement of the Constitution, no Bill or amendment relating to the language of the Supreme Court and the High Courts could be introduced in either House of Parliament without the previous sanction of the President.
2. Under Article 343(3) of the Constitution, Parliament may by law provide, for the purposes specified therein, for the use of the Devanagari form of numerals.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Article 349 barred, for the first fifteen years, any Bill or amendment on Supreme Court and High Court language without the President previous sanction, and Article 343(3) lets Parliament provide for the Devanagari form of numerals for specified purposes.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Section 5 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a translation in Hindi of a Central Act or Ordinance, published under the authority of the President in the Official Gazette, is deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi.
2. Under Section 6 of the Official Languages Act, 1963, a translation in Hindi of an Act passed by the Legislature of a State in a language other than Hindi, published in the Official Gazette of the State under the authority of the President, is deemed to be the authoritative text thereof in Hindi.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Section 5 of the 1963 Act deems a Hindi translation of a Central Act or Ordinance published under the President authority in the Official Gazette to be its authoritative Hindi text; statement 2 misstates the authority for State Acts under Section 6.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology was set up in the year 1961 and functions under the Ministry of Education.
2. The Central Hindi Directorate was established in the year 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both are correct: the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology was set up in 1961 under the Ministry of Education, and the Central Hindi Directorate was established in 1960.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Department of Official Language was set up as a separate department in the Ministry of Home Affairs in the year 1975.
2. The Committee of Parliament on Official Language was constituted in the year 1976.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the Department of Official Language was set up as a separate department in the Ministry of Home Affairs in 1975, and the Committee of Parliament on Official Language was constituted in 1976.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first Official Language Commission, appointed in 1955 under the chairmanship of B. G. Kher, submitted its report to the President in the year 1956.
2. The Presidential Order based on the recommendations of the first Official Language Commission, issued after considering the report of the Committee of Parliament, was issued in the year 1960.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 2 only
options.B: 1 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: the first Official Language Commission under B. G. Kher, appointed in 1955, reported in 1956, and the Presidential Order on its recommendations, after the parliamentary committee report, was issued in 1960.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Town Official Language Implementation Committee is constituted in a town or city which has ten or more Central Government offices.
2. The Central Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: a Town Official Language Implementation Committee is formed in a town or city having ten or more Central Government offices, and the Central Official Language Implementation Committee is chaired by the Secretary, Department of Official Language.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar of the Department of Official Language is awarded to Ministries/Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks for excellence in implementing the Official Language Policy.
2. The Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield is awarded to the Zonal Railway adjudged the best in the implementation of the Official Language Policy.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both are correct: the Rajbhasha Kirti Puraskar goes to Ministries, Departments, public sector undertakings and nationalised banks, and the Rail Mantri Rajbhasha Shield goes to the Zonal Railway adjudged best, for Official Language implementation.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Rajbhasha Bharati', the quarterly journal devoted to the Official Language and its implementation, is published by the Department of Official Language.
2. The 'Brihad Prashasan Shabdavali' (Comprehensive Glossary of Administrative Terms) is published by the Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Rajbhasha Bharati is published by the Department of Official Language, and the Brihad Prashasan Shabdavali, the comprehensive glossary of administrative terms, is a Commission for Scientific and Technical Terminology publication.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Hindi Teaching Scheme, the Prabodh course is intended for employees who do not possess any knowledge of Hindi, i.e., beginners.
2. In the Hindi Teaching Scheme, Parangat is the final prescribed course for clerical (ministerial) staff.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Prabodh is the beginners course for employees with no knowledge of Hindi. Pragya, not Parangat, is the final prescribed course for clerical or ministerial staff, so statement 2 is wrong.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Kendriya Hindi Samiti (Central Hindi Committee), the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi, is chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. The Hindi Salahakar Samiti (Hindi Advisory Committee) of a Union Ministry is chaired by the Minister in charge of that Ministry.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both are correct: the Kendriya Hindi Samiti, the highest policy-making body for the progressive use of Hindi, is chaired by the Prime Minister, and a Ministry Hindi Salahakar Samiti is chaired by the Minister in charge of that Ministry.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 120 of the Constitution, a member of Parliament who is unable to express himself adequately in Hindi or English may address the House in his mother tongue with the permission of the presiding officer of the House.
2. Under Article 210 of the Constitution, business in the Legislature of a State shall be transacted in English only.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 1 only
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: Article 120 lets a member unable to express himself adequately in Hindi or English address the House in his mother tongue with the presiding officer permission. Article 210 does not confine State Legislature business to English only.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Hindi Diwas is observed on 14th September because on 14th September 1949 the Constituent Assembly adopted Hindi as the Official Language of the Union.
2. World Hindi Day is observed on 10th January every year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct: Hindi Diwas on 14 September marks the Constituent Assembly adoption of Hindi as the Official Language of the Union on 14 September 1949, and World Hindi Day is observed on 10 January.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The responsibility for ensuring that the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 are issued in both Hindi and English rests with the officer signing the document.
2. Under Rule 12 of the Official Language Rules, 1976, the responsibility for ensuring proper compliance with the provisions of the Official Languages Act and the Rules in a Central Government office rests with the administrative head of the office.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both are correct: the officer signing a Section 3(3) document must ensure it issues in Hindi and English, and Rule 12 of the 1976 Rules makes the administrative head of the office responsible for compliance with the Act and Rules.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Annual Programme for the implementation of the Official Language Policy of the Union is prepared by the Ministry of Home Affairs (Department of Official Language).
2. The Quarterly Progress Report on the progressive use of Hindi is sent by a Central Government office directly to the President's Secretariat every quarter.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: Both 1 and 2
options.B: 2 only
options.C: 1 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Only statement 1 is correct: the Annual Programme is prepared by the Ministry of Home Affairs through the Department of Official Language. Quarterly Progress Reports go to the controlling office or Ministry, not directly to the President Secretariat.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. To ensure that the documents specified in Section 3(3) of the Official Languages Act, 1963 are invariably issued in both Hindi and English, Central Government offices designate certain points in the office, such as the despatch section, which are known as check points.
2. Before visiting a Central Government office for inspection, the Committee of Parliament on Official Language obtains detailed information about the implementation of the Official Language Policy in that office through a prescribed questionnaire filled in by the office.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both are correct: offices designate check points such as the despatch section to ensure Section 3(3) documents issue bilingually, and the Committee of Parliament obtains implementation details through a prescribed questionnaire before inspecting an office.

q: A Central Government office located at Lucknow in Uttar Pradesh issued 500 letters during a quarter, of which 470 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'A' being 90 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'A' being 100 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'A' being 55 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'A'

e: 470 of 500 letters is 94 per cent. Uttar Pradesh is in Region A, where the target for correspondence originating in Hindi is 100 per cent, so the office has fallen short.

q: A Central Government office located at Thiruvananthapuram in Kerala issued 800 letters during a quarter, of which 400 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'C' being 55 per cent
options.B: The office has met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 50 per cent
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for Region 'C' being 40 per cent
options.D: No target applies to offices in Region 'C'

e: 400 of 800 letters is 50 per cent. Kerala is in Region C, where the target for correspondence originating in Hindi is 55 per cent, so the office has fallen short.

q: A Central Government office located at Ahmedabad in Gujarat issued 500 letters during a quarter, of which 460 were originally written and issued in Hindi. With reference to the target prescribed under the Annual Programme, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 100 per cent
options.B: The office has fallen short of the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 95 per cent
options.C: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target for Region 'B' being 92 per cent
options.D: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for correspondence originating in Hindi in Region 'B' being 90 per cent

e: 460 of 500 letters is 92 per cent. Gujarat is in Region B, where the target for correspondence originating in Hindi is 90 per cent, so the office has exceeded the target.

q: During a quarter, a Central Government office recorded 100 notes on files, of which 42 were written in Hindi. With reference to the target fixed under the Annual Programme for noting on files in Hindi, the position is:

options.A: The office has fallen short, the prescribed target for noting in Hindi being 50 per cent
options.B: No target is fixed for noting on files in Hindi
options.C: The office has exceeded the target, the prescribed target for noting on files in Hindi being 30 per cent
options.D: The office has just met the target, the prescribed target being 42 per cent

e: 42 of 100 notes is 42 per cent, which exceeds the Annual Programme target of 30 per cent for noting on files in Hindi.

q: For its Quarterly Progress Report, an office counts its Hindi correspondence. During the quarter it issued 120 letters, of which 48 were originally written in Hindi and 72 were English drafts translated into Hindi before issue. The number to be counted as Hindi correspondence is:
e: Only letters originally written in Hindi count as Hindi correspondence; the 72 English drafts translated into Hindi are excluded, so the count is 48.

q: An accounts clerk passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 67 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 800
options.C: No cash award, the minimum marks required being 70 per cent

e: The Pragya cash award is Rs 1,600 for 60 to 69 per cent marks; 67 per cent falls in that middle slab.

q: A junior accounts assistant passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 56 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 800
options.D: No cash award, the minimum marks required being 60 per cent

e: The Pragya cash award is Rs 800 for 55 to 59 per cent marks; 56 per cent falls in that lowest award slab.

q: A senior accounts assistant passes the Pragya examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 72 per cent marks and applies for the cash award. The amount admissible to him is:

options.A: Rs 800
options.D: No cash award, cash awards being admissible only up to 70 per cent marks

e: The Pragya cash award is Rs 2,400 for 70 per cent or more marks; 72 per cent falls in that top slab.

q: A typist in a Central Government office passes the Hindi typewriting examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 92 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the typewriting examination being 95 per cent or more marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible to him, the prescribed threshold of 90 per cent or more marks for the typewriting examination having been secured
options.C: A cash award is admissible only if he also passes the Pragya examination in the same year
options.D: He becomes entitled to a lumpsum award in lieu of the cash award

e: A cash award for the Hindi typewriting examination is admissible on securing 90 per cent or more marks; 92 per cent crosses that threshold, so the award is payable.

q: A stenographer passes the Hindi stenography examination under the Hindi Teaching Scheme with 84 per cent marks and claims the cash award. The correct position is:

options.A: A cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold being 80 per cent marks
options.B: A cash award is admissible only if his stenography speed exceeds 100 words per minute
options.C: He becomes entitled to personal pay equal to one increment instead
options.D: No cash award is admissible, the prescribed threshold for the stenography examination being 88 per cent or more marks

e: A cash award for the Hindi stenography examination is admissible only on securing 88 per cent or more marks; 84 per cent is below that threshold, so no award is payable.
